subtype: Approach: grabbing it first and refusing to hand over [Pitfall]
passage: Note from Thomas, evening. I want to record what happened today so we can talk to both children. Susan got to the sofa first, picked up the remote and, when her younger brother Suraj asked for it, hid it behind a cushion. "I was here first," she said. Suraj shouted and then cried. My wife and I came in to find both of them red-faced and the remote nowhere to be seen. It was no longer about the television, it was about who was in charge. Neither child watched anything, and the evening was spoilt for everyone. Tomorrow we will sit down together.

qa.q: Where did Susan hide the remote?
qa.a: Susan hid the remote behind a cushion.

qa.q: What might Susan have been feeling when she said 'I was here first'?
qa.a: Susan was probably feeling possessive and defensive, wanting to keep what she got to first.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Susan and Suraj try, and why?
qa.a: They could take turns using a timer or agree on a plan for which days each of them picks. A shared plan means no one has to win by hiding the remote.

qa.q: How does the fight look to Suraj?
qa.a: Suraj shouted and cried when the remote was hidden, so Suraj felt shut out and treated unfairly by an older sister.

grounding: An older sister takes the remote and hides it because she got there first, the brother complains, the parents are upset, and sharing becomes a fight over power.

subtype: Approach: grabbing it first and refusing to hand over [Pitfall]
passage:
Saturday night
Diary, I did a bad thing and I'm still angry. I got to the sofa first this morning, so I took the remote. Vinay wanted his cartoon, and I said, "I came first, didi rule." When he tried to grab it I hid it inside my pillow cover. He cried and told Papa. Papa asked me for the remote and I said I didn't know where it was. Mummy found it. She looked at me like she didn't know me, and that was worse than shouting. Then there was no TV for anyone, all day. Vinay didn't talk to me at lunch. It wasn't even about the cartoon any more. I just didn't want to lose.
- Nandini

qa.q: Where did Nandini hide the remote?
qa.a: Nandini hid it inside a pillow cover.

qa.q: How did Nandini feel when Mummy looked at her after finding the remote?
qa.a: Nandini felt ashamed and hurt, saying that look was worse than shouting, while still feeling angry.

qa.q: Which approach would have suited the siblings better, and why?
qa.a: They could have agreed turns, like one programme each, because a clear rule stops it becoming a fight about who wins.

qa.q: How does the day look to Vinay?
qa.a: Vinay feels cheated and upset, crying when his sister hides the remote, and then stays away from her at lunch.

grounding: It shows an older sister hiding the remote because she got there first, and the sharing turning into a costly fight over power.

subtype: Approach: grabbing it first and refusing to hand over [Pitfall]
passage: In their village above the river, there was one television in Vidya's home, and one remote with a cracked back held together by tape. On Sunday Vidya reached it first and slid it into her kurta pocket. "I'm first, so it's mine," she said. Her little brother Dorjee grabbed at her sleeve. She held her arm up high where he couldn't reach. Their grandmother put down her spinning and asked for the remote. Vidya shook her head. Dorjee wailed. Their father came in from the fields, heard both, took the remote and put it on top of the cupboard. "When you two can share, it comes down." Vidya stared at the dark screen and felt her face go hot.

qa.q: Where did the father put the remote?
qa.a: He put it on top of the cupboard.

qa.q: What was Vidya feeling as she stared at the dark screen?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and hot-faced, and perhaps angry, because holding on to it had cost everyone the television.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it?
qa.a: Vidya turned sharing into a contest of who holds on longest; a simple turn plan with Dorjee would fix it.

qa.q: How does the fight look to their grandmother?
qa.a: Their grandmother sees two children upset and a small thing turning big, so she steps in, and is probably tired and saddened.

grounding: It shows an older sister keeping the remote because she got it first, her brother protesting and the parents stepping in, with a cost to everyone.
